results.summary:
Two files were changed to upgrade Jinja2 and fix all ten security advisories:

1. **requirements.txt** – Jinja2 bumped from 2.11.2 → 3.1.6 (patches GHSA-cpwx-vrp4-4pq7, GHSA-g3rq-g295-4j3m, GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95, GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj, GHSA-q2x7-8rv6-6q7h, and the five PYSEC advisories). MarkupSafe was also updated from 2.0.1 → 2.1.5 to match what Jinja2 3.x requires.

2. **shop/render.py** – In Jinja2 3.x, `Markup` and `escape` were removed from the `jinja2` namespace and now live exclusively in the `markupsafe` package. The import line was updated from `from jinja2 import Environment, Markup, escape` to `from jinja2 import Environment` plus a new `from markupsafe import Markup, escape`. The rest of the logic is unchanged.

All four tests continue to pass after the upgrade.

results.summary: The `requests` library was upgraded from 2.25.1 to 2.33.0 in `requirements.txt`, resolving all eight listed security advisories (GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7, GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56, GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2, GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q, PYSEC-2023-74, PYSEC-2026-1872, PYSEC-2026-1873, PYSEC-2026-2275). The companion `urllib3` pin was also bumped from 1.26.18 to 1.26.20 (latest 1.x patch) to stay on a clean, non-CVE build. No application code needed changing — the project only uses stable `requests` APIs (`Session`, `get`, `raise_for_status`, `json`) that are identical in 2.33.0. All 4 tests pass.

results.summary: The only change required was bumping the urllib3 pin in requirements.txt from 1.26.20 to 2.8.0. No application code needed modification because the project uses urllib3 indirectly through the `requests` library, and the `requests`/`FakeSession` API surface the code relies on is fully compatible with the new urllib3 2.x series. After installing the updated dependencies, all 4 tests passed cleanly. This upgrade resolves all 16 listed security advisories (GHSA-* and PYSEC-*) tied to the vulnerable urllib3 1.26.x release.
